This vignette demonstrates how to handle single-arm trial scenarios, and how to utilize the `endpoint_var` argument to decouple the endpoint grouping from the cure fraction formula.

## The `endpoint_var` argument

In earlier versions, `multimcm` deduced the endpoint grouping variable based strictly on its position in the `cureformula`. This made it impossible to specify models like:
1. A single-arm trial with multiple endpoints.
2. A single shared cure fraction across multiple endpoints.

By using the `endpoint_var` argument, you can explicitly define which column splits the data into multiple survival endpoints, freeing up `cureformula` to model the cure fraction exactly as you want.

### Setup Dummy Data

Let's create a dummy single-arm dataset with two endpoints:

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(multimcm)

set.seed(123)
single_arm_data <- data.frame(
  os = rexp(100, 0.1),
  os_event = sample(0:1, 100, replace=TRUE),
  endpoint_type = sample(c("PFS", "OS"), 100, replace=TRUE),
  bg_rate = 0.01
)
```

## Scenario 1: Single Shared Cure Fraction

If you want a single, pooled cure fraction across all endpoints in a single-arm trial, you just omit the endpoint variable from the `cureformula`.

Because we specify `endpoint_var = "endpoint_type"`, the package knows to jointly model two separate survival distributions, but it will estimate a single `cf_pooled` applied to both!

```{r shared-cf, eval=FALSE}
out_shared <- bmcm_stan(
  input_data = single_arm_data,
  formula = "Surv(time=os, event=os_event) ~ 1",
  cureformula = ~ 1,                        # ~ 1 indicates a single shared cure fraction
  endpoint_var = "endpoint_type",           # Explicitly tell the package the grouping variable
  family_latent = "exponential",
  bg_model = "bg_fixed",
  bg_varname = "bg_rate",
  t_max = 400
)

# You can plot the joint survival:
# plot_S_joint(out_shared)
```

## Scenario 2: Separate Cure Fractions per Endpoint

If you believe the cure fraction varies by endpoint, include the endpoint variable as a fixed effect in the `cureformula`. 

```{r separate-cf, eval=FALSE}
out_separate <- bmcm_stan(
  input_data = single_arm_data,
  formula = "Surv(time=os, event=os_event) ~ 1",
  cureformula = ~ endpoint_type,            # ~ endpoint_type indicates separate cure fractions
  endpoint_var = "endpoint_type",           # Still required to explicitly define the groups
  family_latent = "exponential",
  bg_model = "bg_fixed",
  bg_varname = "bg_rate",
  t_max = 400
)
```

## Scenario 3: Multiple Arms

If you have a traditional multi-arm trial and want to explicitly use `endpoint_var`, the treatment variable simply becomes any fixed effect in `cureformula` that is *not* the endpoint.

```{r multi-arm, eval=FALSE}
multi_arm_data <- single_arm_data
multi_arm_data$treatment <- sample(c("A", "B"), 100, replace=TRUE)

out_multi <- bmcm_stan(
  input_data = multi_arm_data,
  formula = "Surv(time=os, event=os_event) ~ 1",
  cureformula = ~ treatment + endpoint_type, 
  endpoint_var = "endpoint_type",           
  family_latent = "exponential",
  bg_model = "bg_fixed",
  bg_varname = "bg_rate",
  t_max = 400
)
```
